author: m4rine_semperfi
body:
1) Assists
What it looks like:

Reason: Sometimes in team based games it's not always about the final hit, but rather damaging a player so he/she is able to be hit once. Kill stealing is not too common, but this addition would address this as well as be very helpful when you attack an enemy and if he/she runs away, you are able to see if a team mate finished the job or if the player survived. (+1 credit could be removed if deemed to helpful to the player)

2) Killstreaks
What it looks like:

Reason: When you are fighting it can sometimes be nice to see how many kill you are at, the number located to the right of the player name in parenthesis tells how many total players you have killed on your current life.

3) Arrow Hit
What it looks like:

Reason: During a fight where you can't directly see the enemy sometimes arrows can miss and hit other players, so it would be helpful to see which player you are hitting to see if you need to adjust your aim. (Of course these features could be disabled in a custom GUI like /chatsettings or /cs)

replies.author: DaFrozenBlaze
replies.body:
Losing credits to kill stealing is quite insignificant, not worth implementing giving credits to those who assisted in my opinion. 

Kill streak should be counted within a certain amount of time. Like if within the next 10 seconds of the first kill you get another kill, that would be considered a streak. Otherwise people can just camp and get "kill streaks"

It would be nice, but most of the time you would be able to see who you are shooting. When shooting someone very far away, there's really no need to know the person you shot. Someone people may want this, so this is best when it can be toggled. 

Maybe some of these are implemented in Atlas

replies.author: kycrafft
replies.body:
I'm fine with killstreaks/killstreak rewards (as long as they can't be endlessly abused by killfarming to get a billion credits) but I think the other too are a bit trivial. 

Assist: Killstealing is annoying, but it's just something that happens, and a lot of players would rather have the kill for the stats rather than the credits. In addition, there isn't a good system to determine who the assist should be given to. What if I bring a player down to half a heart , but then he heals up to 8 hearts, and someone brings him back down to half a heart, and yet another person gets the kill. Who get's the assist? And what dictates when an assist is given? Should I go around shooting every player on the other team,once in order to farm assists?

Arrow Tag: Target recognition and aim should come down to skill and experience. In my personal opinion, the game shouldn't have to hold your hand all the way through. If I constantly can't tell who I'm hitting, that's my fault and something that I need to learn to fix. 

Meh, just my 2 cents

replies.author: kycrafft
replies.body:
In response to 1)

  •  First, I don't want to think of a good system, because I don't think it's necessary. Also, I'm no expert but running a damage tag counter for assists would probably cause significant lag
  • There would need to be a minimum damage number that Player 1 must exceed in order to give the assist, or my point about running around shooting everyone in the map would still stand. 
  • 45 seconds seems rather long to me; most players will be killed off or heal to full health in half that time, even without gapples. Maybe a 20 second timer would be nice, but this doesn't fix other problems, which I will list below
  • When does the timer reset? If Player 1 does damage and 5 seconds later Player 2 does damage, is the timer reset, and Player 1's damage nullified? Will Player 2 get the assist, even if Player 1 did more damage and hit first? 
  • If the timer does not reset, after Player 2 does damage, then who gets the assist if they both do the same amount of damage? 
2)
  • "You are yet to supply one reason why this is overpowered other than the bland statement that 'you should learn to know who you are hitting and the game is holding your hand.'   ". I did not imply that it was overpowered, I just implied that it is a crutch and shouldn't been needed. In addition, maybe my statement was bland, but it's the truth. People should learn where there arrows are going, whether the server is telling them or not. 
  • The only times you are shooting someone at 60 blocks out tend to be a) if you are trying to shoot down someone bridging or b) just laying down suppressing fire. If you are really trying to kill someone, by arrow damage alone, from 60 blocks out and cannot tell who your arrows are hitting, that's normal. By the nature of Minecraft and Avicus (arrow drop off/gapples/cover/ect) means that you realistically should not be trying to outright kill someone at 60 blocks out under most circumstances. In normal situations the only way you'd be able to kill a player with full health and just with arrows, at that range is if you were a skilled archer in the first place (or just lucky like me). In that case, I would imagine those players would have already developed a feel for the bows to the extent that it really isn't as crucial.
  • Playing with no audio is something that I just don't recommend. I do it some times and it's horrible; it limits awareness severely. I admit that an arrow tag feature would be useful in this instance, but it's still a crutch that players should learn to play without
  • I don't consider it so much of a buff, as I consider it a crutch. It's something that people might fall back on in the absence of putting in the effort to be aware of who they are shooting
  • Sure it's simple, and not too game changing, but again, I can't see it being useful enough for it to be added. Avicus has a lot of shit to fix, and I think we have to focus on that first.

replies.author: Elly
replies.body:
Kill assists are something I've been personally considering for a while now, and I'm interested in looking into good ways to implement it within a plugin. A proper implementation would not actually have to send a database query for every hit by every player, as these calculations could be done within the plugin on the internal server. Then, they could be recorded by the database after a significant event has happened, in this case when the player dies and an assist has been awarded.  
  
To the others, I think a good way of implementing kill assists would be to award an assist to the player, excluding the killer, who'd dealt the highest amount of damage. For the most part, this would prevent people from "assist farming". Even then, I'm not convinced that farming kill assists would be detrimental for a team, as you would still be helping to make the other team easier to kill.  
  
To say that adding kill assists would be easy is an understatement, as it can get resource-intensive for both the internal server and the database, due to the increase of queries. Despite this, there are possible ways to implement them; it's all about picking the most appropriate and efficient way to do it.
